samples.question: The page carries several thin dark threads. All threads have exactly the same dark colour and the same thickness, so colour and thickness say nothing about which thread matters; every pale grey blob is background clutter and must be ignored. Exactly two thread ends touch each of the four sides of the page -- two on the top side, two on the bottom side, two on the left side and two on the right side -- so counting ends on a side cannot settle the question. Threads never touch or cross each other. Exactly one thread runs all the way from one side of the page to a different side; every other thread starts on a side and dead-ends deep inside the page, far from any side. Some dead-ending threads are longer than the thread that gets across, so length does not settle it either: the only way to tell is to follow a thread along its whole length from one end to the other. Report the two sides linked by the single thread that runs from one side to another. Answer ambiguous if more than one thread links two different sides. Which two sides of the page does that one through-thread join?
